prompt: A wide anamorphic-looking photograph, shot from far across a cheap English leisure-centre gym through a long telephoto lens, as if the two men are being watched from the other side of the room. Small in the frame, a thin young man of 22 lies on his back on a worn bench press under a loaded barbell, looking straight up with an open, completely trusting face. He has narrow shoulders lost inside a baggy brown anorak, and a thin patchy moustache that is not working. At the head of the bench stands a tired, heavy-eyed man of about fifty in a grey car coat worn over a faded tracksuit, hands tucked under the bar to spot him, a steel flask on the floor by his feet. Both men are clearly seen and in sharp focus, the lens compressing the room so that rows of dusty cable machines, a rack of mismatched rubber-coated dumbbells and a scuffed wall of mirrors stack up behind them out of focus. Large blocks of empty shadow and bare institutional-green painted wall fill much of the frame. The only real light is a bank of overhead fluorescent tubes, some flickering and dim, so the corners and edges of the frame fall away into murky darkness while the bench glows a flat sickly yellow-green. Muted browns, greys and tired greens, visible film grain, slightly faded colour as if on old 1970s colour film. Nothing has gone wrong yet; the barbell is perfectly still. Thanks.
